utterances.text: Yes. Because his sister and her husband live close by the Zigic house, we invited them over for the barbecue, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What ethnicity was her husband?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Her husband is a Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzebric, when you left for the Zigic house, did Zoran happen to mention any special reason for inviting you over to his house?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: No, there was no special reason. But actually, we said, "Well, let's have a barbecue," because it was a month since I was wounded, so to mark that month since my wounding. We sort of gave a reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you are a machine technician?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have a hobby of any kind?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes. I play the guitar, and actually, I play the guitar professionally now as a means of livelihood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the friend of yours who was with you on the occasion?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: He's also a guitar player, and we played together for a long time, and we have been friends for a long time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether Zoran Zigic played the guitar?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes. Zoran played the guitar with my brother, and it was a group. They had a band called Klas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you arrived in the yard of the house towards dusk, did Zoran leave the yard at any time?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes, he left about twice. Once he went to buy some more drink and some more bread.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived, did anybody else arrive as well?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, the neighbours. Actually, I don't know them, whether they're neighbours or not, but other people did arrive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you actually get the barbecue going?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: It might have been around 10.00, I would say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that when dinner began?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you play the guitar?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: While we were sitting around and getting the barbecue going and the fire going, we played, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Zoran Zigic play?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Zoran tried to play, but he couldn't actually play because of his finger that was bandaged up, and then he was irritated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were sitting in Prijedor before you came to the Zigic house, what did you have to drink?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: I know that I drank beer, but I can't remember. I think we drank beer most of the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what state were you in? Could you see that you were -- had been drinking?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Well, we started at 12.00 and left at 6.00, left for Zigic's house at 6.00, so the alcohol took its toll.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about Zoran's state, what state was he in?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Zoran was the most drunk because he started drinking -- he'd already been drinking before me and my colleague got there. He had already -- he was already tipsy when we got there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this dinner began, did Zoran leave the yard at all?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't. He couldn't because he was drunk, and he just sat around drinking, if I can put it that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After dinner, do you know who left the yard of Zigic's house first?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether anyone went out, but I know that Zigic went into the house. Actually, he was taken into the house because he was drunk, so they almost carried him in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe what you mean, took him off? Did he actually carry him, walk beside him and held him up, or -- describe it to us.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, he held him up, and Ziga leaned against him with his full weight, so actually, he almost carried him in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when Zigic went into the house, what happened? What did he do then?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: He went to sleep straight away because he'd been drinking the whole day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where he lay down?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you stay on in the yard?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes. We stayed on in the yard because there was a curfew in force, so we weren't allowed to go home until after the curfew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how long the curfew lasted, up to what time?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: I think it was up to 5.00 a.m. I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you be more specific as to time? When did Zoran go into the house?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: I think it was around 12.00, midnight. About midnight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you all do after midnight? Did you still sit around?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes. We sat around, played, drank, ate, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anything happen afterwards?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Well, some shooting started in Prijedor like every night. First it was sporadic and later on you could hear stronger gunfire. There was more shooting. And then later on towards dawn the situation was calmer. It became sporadic again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The shooting that you mentioned, is that usual compared to the previous evening or previous evenings?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Well, it was more intensive that particular night, more intensive gunfire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it last longer?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how long the shooting went on for, intensive shooting, I mean?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Well, it went on until almost daybreak. It was almost daybreak when it subsided.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that period of time, that is to say, until you left the Zigic yard, did you enter the house at any time?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes. I went inside two or three times. I went to the toilet and ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Zoran sleeping when you went in?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes. Whenever I went in, he said, "Go on. Go in and see if he's Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25 still alive." That's what they said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the company make any comments that evening linked to the shooting?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, somebody made a remark to the effect, "They're shooting again, and tomorrow they'll again say that it was Ziga's fault," something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were sitting there, did you know the reason for the intensive gunfire?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you leave the Zigics' yard?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: We left the yard when it had dawned, around 5.00 or 6.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the shooting still going on?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Well, you could hear a shot or two but it had subsided.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you left the Zigics' yard, was Zoran in the house? Was he sleeping?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next day when you woke up, did you have any knowledge as to the reason for the gunfire?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: As I went to the Bentley pizzeria again, there was talk that people had rebelled in Keraterm and that they had been captured and that there had been this rebellion in Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they saying that many people had been killed in Keraterm that evening?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, were you in the unit? Were you assigned to a unit?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Because I had been wounded, I was guarding the kindergarten in the Pecani district. I was given guard duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me go back to the Zigics' yard once again. From the moment Zoran went into the house until you left their yard, did you see Zoran come out of the house?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this incident, would you see Zoran Zigic again?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes, occasionally in town a couple of times. And he had a small motorcycle, and when I needed it, I borrowed it from him a couple of times.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm almost through, but would you be kind enough to allow me to put this next question in private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please continue, Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you left the yard or just before you left the yard, your assessment, Zoran Zigic, in view of his intoxicated state, was he capable of getting up and moving around?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: In my opinion, he was not. He was so drunk. In fact, he was non-stop drunk those days, and that night in particular.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my last question. Just in a couple of sentences, could you describe him from that time period, what kind of person Zoran Zigic was, as compared to the prewar period?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: In that period he was a completely different man. He drank a lot. To be quite frank, I avoided him whenever I could. I didn't want to be in his company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he ready to assist in such a condition when he was not drunk?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. All his life he was ready to help. When we were young boys, he would lend me his guitar, and whenever I needed anything, he was always there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. In view of the limited time that we have left, I will end my examination-in-chief there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Deretic. So Witness, you are now going to answer questions by the Prosecution, and it will be Mr. Saxon. You have the floor, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Saxon:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzebric, can you tell us, please, where you served in the army of Republika Srpska, and from when to when?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: From when Prijedor was attacked on the 30th of April until 1996. I can't remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that you were wounded in 1992, I believe it was in June of 1992, and you mentioned that you were wounded in the arms, legs, and chest. Can you be more specific about the nature of those wounds, please?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: The first day that we reached the Gradacac theatre of war, we spent the night in a wood, and already the next day a shell hit us. And there were six or seven of us that were wounded by the shrapnel of the shell that hit me in the legs, arms, chest, and neck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you -- were these deep wounds or were these superficial wounds?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Superficial wounds, mostly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that on the 24th of July, you were in the Bentley cafe with a man named - I won't say his name at this point - and you were with Mr. Zigic, and that you were drinking. You mentioned that Mr. Zigic had a bandage on his left hand. Did Mr. Zigic explain to you how he had hurt his left hand?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't tell me anything, but I had heard that there was a shot or something that cut off his finger.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you're not sure? You don't have personal knowledge of how he hurt his hand?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: No, no. I don't have any personal knowledge. I wasn't present, and I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that after you were drinking at that coffee bar from noon until about 6.00 p.m., you went to the home of Mr. Zigic. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there was a man there named Nikica Janjic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak with Nikica Janjic that night?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: I did. I knew Nikica from our childhood. He's younger than I am. I know him from town, mostly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Nikica Janjic tell you that he had previously been inside the Omarska detention camp where he beat a prisoner in the "white house" by the name of Emir [Realtime transcript read in error "Amir"] Beganovic. Did he tell you that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: No, because I didn't have that kind of a relationship with Nikica at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If I can just note that the English translation says "Amir" Beganovic, and the name I used was "Emir" Beganovic, beginning with a "E."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Jakic mention the Omarska -- Nikica Janjic mention the Omarska detention camp at all during that evening when you were drinking?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Believe me, we talked about all kinds of things, so I can't really say 100 per cent. He probably did. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that you can't recall what you talked about that evening? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: We came there to have fun. We were singing, playing, telling jokes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any recollection of Nikica Janjic talking about any of the detention camps in the Prijedor area at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: I know that Nikica Janjic served in the army in Banja Luka. I know that he went to Banja Luka to serve, to do his military service. But I don't know which unit he belonged to or anything. Believe me, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but that wasn't the question I asked you. It was just a simple question, and I'll ask it again. Do you have any recollection of that evening of Nikica Janjic talking about any of the detention camps in the Prijedor area that existed at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You were drinking beer, and is it fair to assume that Mr. Zigic was also consuming alcoholic beverages that whole time?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just regarding yourself, and would it also be fair to say that you got pretty drunk yourself during that afternoon and that evening?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I could say so. We had a good amount to drink.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you are drunk, is your ability to observe things impaired?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: As I was playing and singing all night, then you -- the alcohol doesn't have the same effect. It has a much lesser effect on one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do we take that answer as a yes or as a no?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you did have to go to the toilet several times that evening. That was your testimony, correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was drinking beer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the alcohol had some physical effect on you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that sometime around midnight, Zoran Zigic went to sleep because he was drunk and he had been drinking all day, and you mentioned that -- I believe your testimony was, "Ziga leaned against him," you used the pronoun "him," when Zigic was being helped inside the house. Who was "him"? Who was helping Zoran Zigic enter the house?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: A dark, tall man. A neighbour of his. He wears a moustache.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that there was a curfew in place in Prijedor at that time. What were the hours of that curfew?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I can't remember exactly, but in any event, we didn't dare go back home before it dawned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that curfew -- did that curfew apply to civilians or to civilians and military personnel together? Who did the curfew apply to?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: It applied to everyone at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Mr. Zigic was inside the house sleeping, and you said that you went inside two or three times to use the toilet --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- did you try to wake Zoran Zigic at any time to ask him if he was okay?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: I would just peep through the kitchen door, see him sleeping on the couch, and go on to the toilet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you try to wake him at all or say anything to him?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a reason why you didn't try to wake him?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: His wife was there, his father and mother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: His wife was where? His father and mother were where?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: They were also there. They were sitting outside with the rest of us. Afterwards, they went into the house too. The parents went first. The wife stayed on with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened in 1992 during that period when there was a curfew in Prijedor when some kind of military necessity arose in the evening, a battle or a fight between opposing forces? Would that curfew still apply?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know. I wasn't -- I didn't have such a post to know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would soldiers have to stay where they were and honour a curfew rather than respond to some military emergency, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know. At the time, I was on guard duty in the kindergarten and that was during the daytime, and that is why I simply don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if you had been on guard duty at that kindergarten at night-time, hypothetically, speaking hypothetically now, and there was an attack near the kindergarten, would you be required to honour the curfew or would you be required to respond to the attack?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, what is your objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The objection is simply that this is a hypothetical assumption. It's an impossible assumption, because the witness has said that he didn't work during the night. To insist on an answer what would have happened if he had worked at night, in the opinion of the Defence, is out of place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, what I heard was that the witness was working during the day and in the evening he watched the kindergarten. Is that what I understood? No? No. I'm sorry. In any event, my understanding was that the Prosecutor was trying to find out whether there was an obligation for the witness to watch the kindergarten or not, but I'll give Mr. Saxon the floor to respond to the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I think I can rephrase my question in a manner that perhaps will be less confusing to the witness and to all the parties, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the evening during that time in July of 1992, although wherever you were, even though there was a curfew in place, if the Muslim army attacked, were you supposed to stay where you were, stay inside and honour the curfew, or were you supposed to respond as a soldier?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: I received no orders about that, and I don't know how I would have behaved. Would I be called by telephone or by courier or somehow? I really don't know how I would behave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the 24th of July, you had returned to duty; isn't that correct? You were guarding the kindergarten?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you testified that on the evening of the 24th of July, you heard intensive shooting for a period of hours; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as a soldier, you made absolutely no response?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: There were other soldiers who had such responsibilities. I probably would have received a message or an order if I was expected to do something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll move on. You mentioned that after the 24th of July, you saw Zoran Zigic a couple more times and that you borrowed his motorcycle. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this a motorcycle that Zoran Zigic also used to get around Prijedor in the summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's a small motorcycle, a Tomos brand, with small engine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did it work? When you got on it and you started it up, how did you make the motorcycle go forward?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Very simply. These are mopeds with automatic rotation, like a bicycle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you show the Trial Chamber and myself, because I've never ridden a moped, what did you have to do to make this moped go forward?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: There were two pedals and you rotate them. The engine starts, and then on the handle you add the speed, and you have brakes on the pedals. That's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which hand or hands do you add the speeds with?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: It's an automatic engine --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: -- and it changes speeds automatically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So how do you hold the motorcycle and make it go forward?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Simply; like this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you hold your hands up higher so the Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: And I add speed by turning round the handle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anything to adjust speed on the left-hand side of that motorcycle?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: No, only the right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where are the brakes?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: I can't remember just now. Usually there are brakes at the handles and with the pedals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there would be one brake on the left side of the handle and there would be another brake on the right side of the handle; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: And foot brakes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that during the summer of 1992, Zoran Zigic was non-stop drunk in those days.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said, "I avoided him whenever I could." Why?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Because you would have to sit down with him, join him drinking, sit around all day and get drunk. He wouldn't let you leave. Once you sat down with him, you couldn't get up again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell us. I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Because he was drunk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why couldn't you get up and leave?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Because how do I know what he'd do to me then? I was afraid of him, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you afraid that Zoran Zigic might do to you if you got up and left against his wishes? I remind you you're under oath today.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: He could beat me or hit me or -- I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Zoran Zigic force you to go to that barbecue on the 24th of July?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: No, because we started drinking together that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Zoran Zigic force you to remain at that party the entire night between the 24th and the 25th of July?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: He did not force us. I told you, because of the curfew, we didn't not leave until day broke.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Saxon. Mr. Deretic, do you have any additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, no, I do not. Thank you. The Defence has no further questions for this witness, and we said we'd be efficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but Mr. Deretic, you're always free to ask questions if you have any. Judge Fouad Riad has the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Dzebric, good morning.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I have just one question stemming from the last question which the Prosecutor asked you. You said you were afraid to leave the company of Mr. Zigic when you were with him because he might, he might be violent, especially when he was drunk, as you said, most of the time. Did he carry a pistol? Would you be as -- I mean, would your fear go as far as being shot by him, or just slap you or that sort of thing? What -- why would you be afraid, I mean, if he is just hitting you? You are a strong man.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Well, the times were like that. People would carry pistols as a normal occurrence. Everybody had pistols.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Judge Fouad Riad. Madam Judge Wald has the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Mr. Dzebric, just a few quick questions. You told us that you started drinking in the Bentley cafe around noon, and then you went on from there at 6.00 or 7.00 to Zigic's house for a barbecue, that he was taken in to the kitchen asleep or half a sleep or asleep around midnight, but that you stayed on because of the curfew until around 5.00, around dawn. Now, were you drinking beer pretty much through that entire 17-hour period? It's about 17 hours, by my calculation.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, basically, but as I said, we had dinner, we ate, we sang, we drank, we played the guitar. So it wasn't just the drink, it was all of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I understand. But during that entire 17 hours, when principally, say, in the late evening and through the night toward dawn, you never got sleepy yourself? You never dozed off for any period of time, or did you?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't sleep because, quite simply, we didn't have anywhere to sleep, and I was brought there to keep the company going, so I couldn't stop. They brought me to sing and to entertain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Now, could -- you told us that several times after Zigic was brought into the house you, on the way to the bathroom, could see into the kitchen and see him lying there asleep. Could you give us any estimate of the last time, of what time it was the last time you saw him asleep in the kitchen, approximately what time it was? It had to be between midnight and 5.00. I just wondered if you could tell us specific -- well, I know you can't pinpoint the moment, but approximately what time it would be when you made your last trip to the bathroom and saw Zigic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Well, I had to go every, let's say, an hour and a half I had to go to the bathroom, so let's say 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Sometime between 3.00 and 4.00 was the last time you saw him, and then if you say you had to go every hour and a half, the time -- would it be fair to say that the time before that would have been, what, between one and two or -- 1.30 and 2.30, somewhere around there?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I'm just trying to get some -- all right. My last question is, in the Zigic house, could anybody -- I know your testimony about Zigic himself was incapable because -- you thought incapable because of his state of intoxication of getting up, but I'm just asking you as an abstract matter, could anybody have left the Zigic house by another exit and somebody sitting in the backyard would not have been able to see them leave?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know the house, but the three times I went inside, the company said, "Go in and see if he's still alive," that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: But pretty much I understood you to say, tell me if I'm wrong, I understood you to say that the barbecue was in the backyard. Is that -- did I misunderstand that? Was it in the backyard of the house. My basic question was, when you went in -- that you saw them take him into the kitchen which suggested to me, you know, through the back door of the kitchen. I'm just asking whether or not to your knowledge there was a front door or a side door that might not have been visible from the backyard, to your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: As I say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: -- I went into the house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay, all right. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Madam Judge Wald. Mr. Dzebric, you said, if I understood you correctly, that Zigic was absent because he went to sleep, in to sleep straight away. Did I understand that properly?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Well, basically, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why did you say go to sleep straight away, immediately, and how did you know?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Because he started dozing off in the yard. He had already started to doze off and drop off, and then they said, "Go on, go in and sleep."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you actually saw him leave, and then you concluded that he was going to sleep; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Afterwards you went into the house, indoors several times to go to the toilet. How many times, if you can tell us, how many times did you go in?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Three times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Three times, you say. Very well. Do you know how much beer you had, how many bottles, how much beer?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't really say. I don't know. I don't know, I really don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in the course of those 17 hours that Judge Wald mentioned and calculated, how many beers -- you say you don't know. You don't know exactly how many beers you had in that period of 17 hours?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: While we were sitting in the coffee bar and while we were paying for the beer, we drank more slowly. We drank much less when we had to pay for it. But when we went to the house, there was a whole lot of beer, but there was a lot of us in the yard as well. So I can't tell you the exact quantity, but there were a lot of us to share out the beer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did Mr. Zigic buy enough beer for all those people for all that time?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Well, I think there was enough to drink. I don't think anybody was lacking. There was a sufficient quantity. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How many people were there, more or less, at the barbecue?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Well, about 15, ten or 15. I can't give you an exact number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fifteen people, right. When did you arrive, approximately, for the barbecue?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: We arrived there at about 7.00 or 8.00. About 8.00 p.m., I would say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 8.00 p.m. to 7.00 in the morning, that would make it about 12 hours, and beer for 15 people during that time. Now, when you went inside, indoors, into the Zigic house, did you have to pass by the kitchen or not?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: No, because that -- the kitchen is to the right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So in order to see Mr. Zigic, you would have to go to the kitchen to see him to do that; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I could see through the door, through the doorway. I peered through the doorway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay, very well. How many people stayed on in the yard after Mr. Zigic went inside to sleep?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Well, everybody else, all the others, and then later on they would leave. The neighbours left. I can't quite remember which order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who stayed on last, to the last? Who were the last people to leave, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Well, I myself and my friend. My friend came with me. Because we were the only ones that had to wait for the curfew to end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you stayed until the end and you were the last people to leave; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes, we will to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another question, if I understood you correctly, you said that the fact that you had been wounded a month prior to that was a good reason to celebrate and to have the barbecue; is that right? Did I understand you to say that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. We -- just sort of pretext, and then I sort of came out with that as a pretext for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the fact that you were wounded was a good motive, a good pretext, reason. Did you notice whether Mr. Zigic had been wounded at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And he had a bandage on his left hand? You said that.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Yes. The fact that I had stayed alive, that I had survived, that was the reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But what about Mr. Zigic? He was wounded as well. He might have been dead as well. So did you not -- were you not curious enough to ask him what had happened to his hand?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: I can't quite remember now what he told me about his finger, whether he said it was a bullet. I really don't know. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But I am asking you whether you had asked him what had happened with his hand. Did you ask him? Did you ask him anything about his hand?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: He might have spoken about it, but I was playing. I was busy playing, and some things I would hear. Others I couldn't hear because I was playing and playing. I really don't know. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but I think that you met in the coffee bar, and so that's why I'm interested. And also at the end you said that you were a guitar player and Mr. Zigic was a guitar player too. So weren't you curious -- on your part, weren't you curious in knowing, "What are you going to do now? Are you capable of playing the guitar?" Did you ask him that? Did you ask him, "Can you play the guitar now?"

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: Well, he tried to play the guitar. He did try that night to play the guitar, but he couldn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But while you were still in the coffee bar, the cafe where you met, did you ask him whether he could still play the guitar?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DZEBRIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Witness Dzebric, we have no further questions to ask you. We thank you for having come and wish you a pleasant journey back and success in your work. I shall now ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that we could take our lunch break at this point. We adjourn for luncheon for 50 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The Defence for Zoran Zigic calls our ninth witness, Mr. Drago Bosancic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Bosancic. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please read the solemn declaration that the usher is giving you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Thank you very much for coming. You will first be answering questions put to you by Mr. Deretic, after that, questions from the Prosecution and the Judges. Mr. Deretic, your witness. Examined by Mr. Deretic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bosancic, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you be kind enough to introduce yourself, your full name and surname.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: My name is Drago Bosancic. I was born on the 14th of January, 1962, in Prijedor. In 1962.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your occupation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: I am a highly-skilled car mechanic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your ethnicity and religion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: I am a Serb of Orthodox faith.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bosancic, after the war started in the area of the Prijedor municipality, were you mobilised?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was, on the 29th of April to the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you were mobilised, where were you deployed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: I was assigned to providing security of the police station building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which town?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: In the town of Prijedor, downtown Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when power was taken over in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the 30th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when the town of Prijedor was attacked?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes. The attack occurred on the 30th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What year?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a reserve policeman, do you have any knowledge whether there were any killed soldiers and policemen during the attack on Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know in the period between the takeover of power and the attack on Prijedor, were there any armed incidents?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the takeover of power, do you know which was the first armed incident in Prijedor municipality? Just a moment. Make a pause, please. You may proceed now.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: There was the murder of a boy called Radenko Djapa the same night that power was taken over. Prijedor was attacked not from the old town but from the direction of Puharska against the Pecani neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what Radenko Djapa was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: He was a member of the Prijedor police force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who killed him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact name, but I know it was a Muslim from Puharska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you heard of investigation centres within Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which were those investigation centres?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: They were Keraterm, Trnopolje, and Omarska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when they were formed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: They were formed immediately after the attack on Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what their purpose was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Their purpose was for people who were not loyal to the new authorities that had taken over power and who had attacked the town and weapons were found on them or had directly participated in the attack, these people were taken to the police station for interviews, after which they were taken to these reception centres or camps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they interrogated there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to them later?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: I don't know while they were in the camps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether any of them were released after interrogation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After these investigation centres were set up, did you continue working on the security of the police station building in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: No. I was transferred to the assistant driver of the vehicle on duty in the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was that car referred to in the vernacular?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: It was known as the Marica, the Black Maria police van.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bosancic, do you know Zoran Zigic? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since when have you known him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: I've known him from before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you used to work before the war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: In the Tomasica mines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you go to work?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: I was transported from the railway station where the taxi drivers were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that time period, would you see Zoran Zigic at the railway station?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he doing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: He was a taxi driver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what kind of vehicle he drove in those days?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: I think it was a Pizi ^ or a Lada. Either a Pizi ^ or a Lada.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what colour it was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: I think it was red.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the war broke out within Prijedor municipality would you see Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether he was mobilised?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To which unit was he mobilised?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: He was mobilised to the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In those days, how was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: He had a camouflage uniform and he wore a red beret and Ray-Ban sunglasses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember during that time period was there anything else that was conspicuous on Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes. He carried a Scorpio weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether he had a bandage on any part of his body?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes, one hand. One hand was bandaged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you were transferred to a new duty, that is, you escorted the driver of the police van, did you have occasion to go to Keraterm, Trnopolje, and Omarska in that vehicle?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why would you go there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: We were taking people there upon the orders of the duty officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you be more specific with the time period when you were assigned to this new duty and when you performed these duties and until when you performed them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: I was doing security from the takeover, that is, the 30th, until about the 20th or 25th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember when you became the driver's escort, when you were assigned to this new duty? Was it before or after the attack on Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Before the attack on Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On those occasions when you went to these three investigation centres, did you have occasion to see Zoran Zigic there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him at all in that time period?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge that Zoran Zigic as a member of the reserve police force came to the police station?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you see him there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bosancic, do you know anything at all related to the incident in Keraterm when a large number of people were killed in one night?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when this incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: The night between the 24th and the 25th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you give us the date, the month, and the year.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: The 24th to the 25th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which month and which year?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that before the takeover -- I'm sorry, before the attack on Prijedor or after the attack on Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: After the attack on Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was the attack on Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: On the 30th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was on the 24th to the 25th of which month?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: June. July, sorry, sorry. Between the 24th and 25th of July, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bosancic, how do you remember that date, the date that you just mentioned? Is there something that makes you remember it, something special?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Well, I was working that night at the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What shift were you on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: It is the third shift, from 9.00 at night till 7.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened that night?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: We learnt about it in the morning when we were to hand over duty to the next shift.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in the police station that night?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether there were any telephone calls during the night?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: There were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember when the first phone call came?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the call from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: From Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you answer the telephone then, or did somebody else pick up the receiver?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: The officer on duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you what had happened? Did he convey to you his telephone conversation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough to tell us briefly what it was about.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: He walked into the room where we were sitting, and he said to the driver on duty, "Take the police van and go to Keraterm. The porters and guards are calling and saying that something is happening over there."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to Keraterm after that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was with you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: The police van driver and myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time was it when you reached Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: About 12.30.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was there when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: We were seen in by a man of some 55 to 60 years of age.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived in Keraterm, was it daytime or nighttime? For the transcript, to make things clearer.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: It was nighttime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that after midnight?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes, after midnight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When that person greeted you, did you have a conversation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us briefly what he said?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: He said that the persons who were in detention were rebelling. We didn't want to get out of the van because we didn't know those people. They were elderly people. We opened the window, switched off the engine. The man accompanied us all the time, and he was asking for reinforcements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you entered Keraterm, where did you park the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Opposite the weighing machine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a hut next to the weighing machine?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far was your vehicle from the weighing machine?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: A couple of metres. There is the weighing machine and the hut containing the weighing machine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you just said you didn't see the hut and now you said that there was the scales and the hut, which is correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Well, there's a hut and from that hut you check the weighing process.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far was your vehicle from the weighing machine and the hut?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: A couple of metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you switched off the engine of the vehicle when you arrived.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear any yelling or shouting or anything at all in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: We did. We heard thumping and singing by the detainees. They were saying "Allah-u-ekber" and things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this conversation that you had with this man, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: We moved forward in a semicircle and went back to the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, when you reached the compound, was the Keraterm compound lit up?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Well, so-so, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Within the Keraterm compound did you see Zoran Zigic then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay there with your vehicle parked?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Ten minutes or so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could it be that Zoran Zigic was there in the compound without you noticing him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: If Zigic had been there, we would have got out of the van, or if he had seen the van, he would have approached us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: We didn't want to get out of the van because there were some elderly people whom we didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean that Zigic was not there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: He was not there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you returned to the police station, what happened next?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: The driver on duty informed the duty officer and I went to the building next door to rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to whether the duty officer undertook anything or took any steps in response to this information?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go to rest?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: The building next door, in the basement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Until 6.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that did you go back to the duty room?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you meet the duty officer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the duty officer say anything at all to you after that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: He told me and the driver on duty that there was chaos in Keraterm and there was a dilemma as to whether we should wait for the next shift or not, but we insisted that he let us go to check things out, to see what had happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to Keraterm after that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time was it when you arrived in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: It was about 7.00, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see in Keraterm when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: We saw people washing down the pista with a hose from the hydrant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you come with that same police van that you were there after midnight in?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you park it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: By the weighing machine. The same place we were parked the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody meet you there on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody come up to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the general mood, the atmosphere of the place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Well, people were washing the pista. We saw parts of clothing, sneakers, things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see bodies on the pista?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any blood on the pista?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was the pista being washed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Allegedly because of the blood that was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Upon your arrival in Keraterm, was it already daylight?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the morning like?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: How do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it raining?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: No, it wasn't raining. It was a brisk morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived, did you see Zoran Zigic there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Several minutes, because nobody came up to us. And to tell you the truth, we were afraid of those people we didn't know, so we went back straight away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You and the driver, did you get out of the van at all?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you entered the Keraterm compound, did you see a Schlepper truck of any kind?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go when you left the Keraterm compound?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: We went back to the police station to hand over our shift.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you meet the duty officer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell him anything in connection with what you had seen and noticed in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Well, the driver on duty started telling him about it, and he said, "Yes, I know, and I have to write an official report." And he was in a general state of panic because he had to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything else in relation to the events in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that that morning you didn't see Zoran Zigic, neither did you see him the first time you went there. After this occurrence in Keraterm, did you ever see Zoran Zigic again?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: That was around the 19th or 20th of August for the holy day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said the holy day, which one?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Well, it's when a great Serbian saint is celebrated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: I saw him in the Gomjenica neighbourhood. The day was the transfiguration day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you working at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes, I worked the second shift.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you happen to find yourself in Gomjenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: We received a report that there was shooting, and the duty officer told me and the driver to go there. They heard that there was some soldiers there and that we should go and find out what it was all about, what was happening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived on the spot, what did you find there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: I saw Zoran Zigic and another soldier lying down on the road, and that was the first time I saw Zigic without his red beret and his Ray-Ban sunglasses and bloody, at that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what time it might have been? Was it in the morning, the afternoon, or in the evening?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: It was sometime in the afternoon, about 3.00 or 3.30 p.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion, did you see any injuries to Zigic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: He had received an injury to his chin because the young boy had shot at him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who shot at Zigic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: A soldier, actually, with a sniper. He had a sniper, and he shot at him, and he -- his Ray-Ban sunglasses and his beret fell off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that man present?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was there, and so was the command of the police station in Gomjenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, there seems to be a mistake in the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, would you tell us once again, where did you see the sunglasses and the beret?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: On that young soldier. He took them away from Zigic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that Zigic was covered in blood?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see the blood?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: It was a wound. You couldn't wash it, and I took -- and he went to wash it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the wound?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Here, underneath his lower lip on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you turn up on the spot in Gomjenica? Why did you go there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Well, the people phoned to say there was shooting, and the duty officer told us to go and check it out, to see what was happening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, did you need to take anybody into custody?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Well, we were to take Zigic and the other one lying down on the ground in. We thought that they had done the shooting, and we thought we'd have to take them in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that what you actually did?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: The commander of the police station did not let Zigic go to the main centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that person's name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Can I say it openly, in open session?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, may we just move into private session for a few moments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, let us move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just have two or three more questions, Mr. President, for this witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this occurrence, did you see Zoran Zigic at all?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you see him and where?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: I saw him in the evening in front of the -- in the fast-food restaurant, sitting there, and it's near the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that on the same day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how much time had elapsed from the Gomjenica event?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Well, it was three or four hours later that I saw him sitting there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice whether Zigic had any blood on him then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: No. He just had a Band-Aid on his chin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record, could you tell us where the fast-food restaurant was located -- where the plaster was located. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: It was on -- to the right of his chin below his lower lip.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my last question: Your opinion about Zoran Zigic from those days? What was he like?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Well, I could tell you a great deal about Zoran Zigic. He was a wonderful man but until he drank. When he drank, it was better to steer clear of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Deretic. Witness, you are now going to answer questions put to you by the Prosecutor, and it will Mr. Waidyaratne, I think, but before that, I see Mr. Krstan Simic on his feet. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just have one question for the witness. Cross-examined by Mr. K. Simic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bosancic, in the area of Urije, was there a reserve police station?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Krstan Simic. Mr. Waidyaratne, your witness. Let me inform you at this point that we shall have to end the day's business by a quarter to three, and please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Sorry, quarter to three?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, a quarter to three.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: May I clarify, is it that I have 15 minutes for cross-examination, Your Honour, if I may correct myself?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. Waidyaratne. That just means that we shall have to finish for the day today at quarter to three. I haven't done the calculations, but I think you have three-quarters of an hour, which means that you will begin the cross-examination today and complete it tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you. Cross-examined by Mr. Waidyaratne:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bosancic, could you tell the Chamber as to what you were -- as to where you were employed prior to your mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: The Tomasica mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you employed in Tomasica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: In the workshop of Tomasica, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you been to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the war have you been to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your occupation in the mine?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: I was a mechanic for the dumpers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your full name is Drago Bosancic. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us as to what it is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Braco, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during -- after the takeover in 1992, you were in the Prijedor Police Station as a reserve policeman. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were assigned to be the driver or the assistant driver to a vehicle which took people from, if I may say, people from the police station to the camps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You took many detainees from the police station to Omarska camp, the Keraterm camp, and the Trnopolje camp; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said during this time that you were -- during this assignment the duty officer ordered you. Can you tell us --

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- the duty officer, who is this duty officer? Is he a senior person in the police station?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: I'm -- no.
