utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bosancic, who was the commander in that police station?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Simo Drljaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Commander of the police station was Simo Drljaca? Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: He was the commander, the chief. The duty officer, the head of the shift, was another man who ordered me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was your immediate commander in the police station?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: In order to say the name, can we go into a private session?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a reason? Do you really need to go into private session? There is nothing -- because there is not much testimony to this event.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: I don't want to name the man openly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Private session, Your Honour, very briefly, only for this question. I'm sorry to have caused any inconvenience. The witness requests it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Let us move into private session. We authorised the Defence to proceed in the same manner, but it is a public hearing. Never mind. Let us move into private session for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session. Please proceed, Mr. Waidyaratne.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, on many occasions you took people from the police station after you said they were interviewed, am I correct, to the camps? You used the word "interview."

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who interviewed these people in the police station?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: The inspectors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you took these people into your van, did you see them beaten and with injuries?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any of those instances you have not seen anybody with injuries, people whom you transported, the detainees, to the camps?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: I was the assistant driver, and it was my job to be inside already, to sit in the car. And as I knew a lot of people, I didn't like to look.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bosancic, do you know a person by the name of Mr. Kugic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know a person by the name of [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you transported these people. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Not Kugic, [redacted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during these trips, have you at any instance seen these people who were being transported to the camps, after they were interviewed in the police stations, with injuries?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll move on, thank you. Now, you said that you knew Zoran Zigic before the war and during the conflict and also after. Now, when you saw Mr. Zoran Zigic in the camouflage uniform and a red beret, could you tell the Chamber as to what colour this camouflage uniform was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: He had a green camouflage uniform and a red beret. That's what he wore all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever seen Mr. Zoran Zigic in a blue-coloured camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, another question with regard to the detainees. You said that you took these detainees and you were in the van. Who -- could you tell the Chamber as to who you handed over these people to, the detainees. When you took them to the camp, whom did you hand them over to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: When we arrived, the driver on duty goes outside and hands them over. I stay in the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Bosancic, you are a person who has made many trips. Have you at any instance known or come to know as to whom this person, the driver, or the person who handed over the prisoners, hand over -- to whom he hands over, hand these people -- handover these people to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Well, he hands them over to the commanders of the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, these commanders --

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Or komandir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, who are these commanders? Did you know any persons? Because you made many trips to the camps, did you know any of these people?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were they? In Omarska, who were the commanders?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: I knew Zeljko Meakic, I knew in Keraterm the late uncle Ziza Knezevic, and I knew Slobodan Kusovic, the teacher in Trnopolje, and I knew them from before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when these commanders were not there or if they were not available or not present, to whom would you hand over the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Probably to some of the inspectors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the inspectors right throughout there in the camps?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, they were there right throughout, 24 hours; is that your position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Well, no, but during the day they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in Keraterm, did you know, other than Mr. Knezevic whom you named, any other person whom you had gone and handed over people?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Omarska, have you seen or come to know any other persons whom you all have handed over detainees?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: I did not hand them over. The duty person handed them over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see as to whom this duty person handed over?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you went to these camps, how long did you spend when you took the detainees from the police station?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Five or ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your position is that you did not spend much time when you took these people, the detainees, during your trips to these three camps; is that your position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So even if we had -- for you to see Mr. Zoran Zigic in any of these camps, this would have been during the -- it would have been during this time, this short time; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: Well, when Zigic saw the policeman -- the police van, if he was there, he would come up to it to see who was inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we'll take, for instance, Keraterm for an example. When you went to Keraterm or took prisoners to Keraterm, did Mr. Zoran Zigic -- how many times would Mr. Zoran Zigic would come to -- did he come to the police van and speak to you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: I didn't see him at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, before I asked my question [as interpreted], the witness repeated that he had never seen Zigic when he drove the detainees, in none of the investigation centres, and the witness answered the question before I raised my objection. And I really do think that the questions are not in order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed, Mr. Waidyaratne.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you. My understanding was that in direct examination that he said, but I will clarify that position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bosancic, have you seen Mr. Zoran Zigic in Keraterm at any time? In the Keraterm camp I'm talking about, the Keraterm camp.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen Mr. Zoran Zigic in Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said - if I'm wrong you may correct me - if I understood you correctly, you said if the van goes -- if he says the police van, that he would come up to the van and speak to you. Did that happen at any time when you went to any of these camps?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC
utterances.text: It did not happen in the camps, but in town. If he saw me in a police car, Zigic would come up to me, and if he was sober, he would help us if we were involved with some person or other.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see the time is quarter to three.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Very well. We're going to stop there for the day. I am still -- yes, Ms. Susan Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Forgive me. I don't mean to hold you up. I just wanted to remind the Chamber that we went from one witness to the other quickly, and I did want, perhaps at the end of all these witnesses, to move one document into evidence from Witness DD/5, but I can do that tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Just a moment, please, because we really do need to adjourn. We reconvene tomorrow, but I'm going to ask the usher to escort the witness out of the courtroom first.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm still waiting for a present from the Prosecution to complete everything, Ms. Susan Somers. But at any rate, Mr. Waidyaratne, you will have half an hour tomorrow. So let us adjourn for the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
